Pull request

What changed, and why

Closes
------

<!-- Every defect is fixed on a branch, through a pull request, and the pull
     request closes the issue it fixes.

     Put Closes #123 in a COMMIT BODY, not only here. That trailer is what
     closes the issue on merge and what permanently links the issue to the
     commit that fixed it - a reference that survives the pull request being
     squashed, retitled, or rewritten years later. A number typed only in this
     description closes the issue and leaves no trace in git.

     One commit per issue, even when several ride the same pull request, so
     any one of them can be reverted alone.

     No issue? Say so. Feature work and chores do not need one. -->

Closes #

How it was tested

     and why - "no Docker locally, so the database-backed jobs are CI's word"
     is a useful sentence; silence is not. -->

Checklist
---------

- [ ] One logical change. Unrelated fixes belong on their own branch.
- [ ] Commits follow Conventional Commits (https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (type(scope): summary).
- [ ] Closes #N is in a commit body for every issue this fixes.
- [ ] Tests come with the change. A bug fix includes a test that fails without it.
- [ ] Every .md touched has its .txt twin updated in the same commit.
- [ ] User-facing changes are documented in this pull request, not a follow-up.
- [ ] No secrets, tokens, or real addresses in the diff, test fixtures included.

     limitations stated here are far cheaper than the ones found later. -->
